newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks slide, no imminent recovery seen.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks slide, no imminent recovery seen.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued to slide on Tuesday and traders said political concerns holding back investors could restrain the possibility of an imminent market recovery.
"Investors may be waiting for the results of the presidential election and to see if the reintegration of Eastern Slavonia passes smoothly," said one trader with a large market share.
The poll is scheduled for June 15 and the United Nations peacekeepers should withdraw from the last Serb-run enclave of Eastern Slavonia in mid-July.
"Another acute problem of the Croatian market is the lack of fresh and interesting stocks," said Denis Fuduric, trader at IB Austria.
Eleven of 15 active stocks fell, three rose and one was flat. Volume doubled to 11,197 shares from Friday and turnover was six times higher at 12.1 million kuna.
Traders said some stocks could dip further this week, although some thought prices had hit bottom and would end their slide. But they agreed no fresh market boom was yet in sight.
Fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka lost 45 kuna to 2,005 but it was the most active issue on volume of 5,025 shares. Drugs firm Pliva inched down eight kuna to 440, with 610 units sold.
"I see this as Zagrebacka's and Pliva's seasonal oscillation and I expect them to recover in due time," Fuduric said.
Another fully-listed stock, Varazdinska Banka ordinary A-series which was split 160-1 and reissued at 100 kuna, resisted the downward trend, rising over 10 percent to 270 kuna.
But traders said the split would not significantly boost the trade with Varazdinska because its share supply is relatively small and the bank is not interesting to foreign investors.
Tuesday's top gainer Croatia Banka edged up 15 kuna to 145, selling 68 units.
Biggest decliner shipper Jadroplov fell 25 kuna to 95, with 587 shares sold.
Food processor Podravka dipped five kuna to 260, selling 608 shares. But traders expected a renewed interest for the stock soon.

"Its fall is due to rumours about its bad 1996 results. But if we see such results were caused by Podravka getting rid of its loss-making subsidiaries, we can forecast a long-term recovery," Fuduric said.
